content: Hypromellose is an ophthalmic solution approved by the FDA for the treatment of eye dryness and for preventing further irritation. Common adverse reactions include eye pain and changes in vision. For adult patients, the FDA-labeled indications include relieving dryness of the eye, temporarily alleviating discomfort caused by minor eye irritations or exposure to wind and sun, and serving as a protectant against further irritation. The recommended dosage is to instill 1 or 2 drops into the affected eye(s) as needed. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of hypromellose in both adult and pediatric patients, whether guideline-supported or not. Similarly, there is limited information on its FDA-labeled use in pediatric patients. Contraindications for hypromellose are not well-documented in the drug label. Warnings include that it is for external use only, and the product should not be used if the bottle tip is broken or punctured, or if the solution changes color or becomes cloudy. To avoid contamination, users should not touch the tip of the container to any surface and should replace the cap after use. If eye pain, changes in vision, continued redness or irritation, or worsening of the condition occurs, or if symptoms persist for more than 72 hours, the user should discontinue use and consult a physician. If the product is swallowed, medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center is advised immediately. Adverse reactions reported during clinical trials include eye pain and changes in vision. Postmarketing experience data is limited. Information on drug interactions is also limited. There is no FDA guidance on the use of hypromellose in specific populations, including pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, specific gender or racial populations, or patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no guidance for its use during labor and delivery, or in immunocompromised patients. Hypromellose is administered as an ophthalmic solution. Monitoring guidelines for its use are not well-documented. There is also limited information on IV compatibility, chronic overdose, pharmacology (mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology), and clinical studies. The product should be stored at room temperature (15°–30°C or 59°–86°F) and should not be frozen. Users are advised to keep the box for complete information. When using this product, users should avoid touching the tip of the container to any surface and replace the cap after use. If swallowed, medical help should be sought immediately. Alcohol interaction with hypromellose has not been established, and patients should consult their doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while using this medication. The brand name for hypromellose is GenTeal®. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names for hypromellose.
